questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

You will not learn cycling __unless you don't try.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__unless you try__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Unless you don't try'** is wrongly used.
 
• 
 You use unless to introduce the only circumstances in which an event you are mentioning will not take place or in which a statement you are making is not true.

 **Examples:**

 
 
• 
 *We cannot understand disease unless we understand the person who has the disease.*
 
 
• 
 *I'm not happy unless I ride or drive every day.*
 
 
 
 
• **Unless’** expresses a condition and is always used in the** negative sense.**
 
• **‘Not’** is never used with ‘**unless**’ as it leads to double negatives making it superfluous.
 
 
• Example: *Unless you study diligently, you'll never understand trigonometry.* 
 
 

**Thus the correct sentence will be: ***You will not learn cycling **unless you try.__***

Mohit did not (1) went to school (2)yesterday as he (3) was unwell. (4)

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Rahul said to his mother, "Can I go out and play now?"

options.text: Rahul asked to his mother could he go out and play now.
Rahul asked his mother that could he go out and play then.
Rahul asked his mother if he could go out and play then.
Rahul asked his mother if can he go out and play now.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rahul asked his mother if he could go out and play then.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

The given sentence is an **interrogative statement in Direct speech**. It needs to be changed in Indirect speech.

When we change the direct speech to indirect speech, the following changes take place:

 
• The Reporting Verb **'said to'** changes to **'asked'.**
 
• Inverted commas are omitted and the **question mark is replaced with a full stop.**
 
• **'If/whether' is added** when it changes from direct to indirect mode.
 
• Modal auxiliary **'can' changes to 'could'.**
 
• The personal pronoun **'I' changes to 'he'.**
 
• Time phrase changes from **'now' to 'then'.**

Following the rules of conversion, the indirect speech sentence will be: ***Rahul asked his mother if he could go out and play then.***

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Fortunately, the fire did not cause much damage.

options.text: Fortunately, not much damage is caused by the fire.
Fortunately, not much damage was caused by the fire.
Fortunately, not much damage was being caused by the fire.
Fortunately, not much damage is being caused by the fire.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fortunately, not much damage was caused by the fire.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

The given sentence is in **Active Voice**. Its structure is: **Adverb + subject + auxiliary verb + negative marker + main verb + object**

It needs to be changed in **Passive Voice**. Its structure will be: **Fortunately + negative marker + Object + helping verb + V3 + by + Subject.**

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Fortunately, not much damage was caused by the fire.*

**Rules of Conversion from Active to Passive Voice:**

 
• Identify the subject, the verb and the object: S+V+O
 
• Change the object into subject
 
• The active verb does not have an object. Therefore, the passive form should begin with **you.**
 
• Change the verb into past participle of the verb
 
• Change the subject into object

Other options are therefore incorrect as it does not follow the rules of conversion.

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. These baits were temptations that people couldn't resist.

B. He evolved a theory that the world was a rat-trap.

C. Once, a peddler sat looking at his rat-traps.

D. Here, people lay baits for others.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

**When we connect the sentences it is important to establish a connection between them.**

The sentences here talk about a man who is unhappy and dejected about the situation around him.

 
• **Sentence C** introduces us to the subject **'a peddler'** where he analyzes his rat-traps.

 *Rat-traps is an unpleasant situation with no prospect of improvement.*
 
• **B follows C.** He evolved a theory that the world was a rat-trap.
 
• **DA follows as a pair.** It states that people lay (baits) traps for others such that people could not resist.
 
• **Thus the correct order is CBDA.**

*Once, a peddler sat looking at his rat-traps. He evolved a theory that the world was a rat-trap. Here, people lay baits for others. These baits were temptations that people couldn't resist.*
